summary: This program adds two more stream calculations to the farmers market inventory: one totals every product price, and one averages the price of just the organic products. Both rely on mapToDouble, which turns a stream of objects into a stream of plain double numbers that knows how to do arithmetic.

lines.text: Collectors is imported because the fuller version of this app in the chapter also groups and collects results; these two new methods return a single number and do not need it.
A placeholder for the inventory list built earlier in the chapter. To run this file yourself, declare a List<MarketProduct> named products here and add a few items, some organic and some not.
The stream work is kept in its own method so main stays readable: ask for the number, then print it.
String.format with %.2f rounds the raw double to two decimal places, which is what money should look like on screen.
Taking the list as a parameter and returning a double keeps this method reusable and easy to test with any inventory.
stream() starts the pipeline: a one-time flow of the list's elements that you can transform without changing the list itself.
This converts each product into its price as a primitive double, producing a DoubleStream that offers numeric operations a normal object stream does not have.
sum() is a terminal operation: it consumes the DoubleStream and hands back the single total.
filter keeps only the elements whose isOrganic() returns true, so everything downstream sees organic products only.
average() returns an OptionalDouble rather than a double, because an empty stream has no meaningful average.
orElse supplies a fallback of 0.0 when there are no organic items, so the caller always gets a usable number instead of an error.
